claims.text: No. In both Python 3.11 and 3.13, `with sqlite3.connect(...) as con` uses the connection context manager for transaction handling; it does not close the connection. The connection must be closed separately.

In both versions, leaving the connection context with no uncaught exception commits the open transaction; an uncaught exception rolls it back and is still raised. If commit fails, rollback is performed. With no open transaction, the manager is a no-op. In 3.13, with `autocommit=False`, a new transaction is implicitly opened after commit or rollback; with `autocommit=True`, the manager does nothing. The 3.13 connect default remains legacy transaction control in this version of the docs.

Close deterministically by explicitly calling `con.close()` after transaction handling, for example in a `finally` block. The 3.13 docs also suggest `contextlib.closing` when a closing context manager is desired. Nest transaction handling inside the closing scope if both behaviors are needed; the connection context manager alone does not close it.
Python 3.13 introduces a documented `ResourceWarning` when a connection is deleted without `close()` having been called. The supplied 3.11 extract does not document that warning.

No. The `autocommit` argument was added in Python 3.12, so code passing it to `sqlite3.connect` cannot be used unchanged on Python 3.11. The 3.13 docs show it as a keyword-only parameter and document the current default as `LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL`.

For code supporting 3.11 and 3.13, first make closure explicit using `try/finally: con.close()` (or use `contextlib.closing` where available), while retaining a separate `with con:` only for commit/rollback behavior. Avoid passing `autocommit` on the shared path; retain the legacy default unless the application deliberately adopts and tests a new transaction policy on supported versions. The supplied extracts establish the API addition in 3.12 and describe 3.13 semantics, but do not fully specify all legacy/default transaction details or prove runtime behavior for every patch release.

note.recommendation: Evidence-backed recommendation: migrate to explicit connection closure independently of transaction scope, using a `finally` close or (on supported runtimes) `contextlib.closing`; use `with con:` inside that closure scope when commit/rollback-on-exit behavior is wanted. Keep `autocommit` out of code that must run unchanged on Python 3.11. If adopting the 3.12+ parameter, choose its transaction mode intentionally and verify application behavior rather than assuming it is a closure mechanism.
unknowns: The extracts do not describe behavior for every intervening or future Python release, nor runtime behavior across SQLite builds.
The 3.11 extract omits an explicit `ResourceWarning` statement; this note only establishes that the supplied 3.13 docs document the warning as added in 3.13.
The extracts do not establish whether the application needs legacy transaction behavior or should migrate to PEP 249-style `autocommit=False`; that depends on its transaction usage.
